sn11.18:0.3: The Worship of Householders (or Sakka’s Worship (1))
sn11.18:1.2: There the Blessed One said this:
sn11.18:1.3: “Bhikkhus, once in the past Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed his charioteer Mātali thus:
sn11.18:1.4: ‘Harness the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds, friend Mātali. Let us go to the park grounds to see the beautiful scenery.’
sn11.18:1.5: - ‘Yes, your lordship,’ Mātali the charioteer replied. Then he harnessed the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds and announced to Sakka, lord of the devas:
sn11.18:1.6: ‘The chariot has been harnessed, dear sir.
sn11.18:1.7: You may come at your own convenience.’
sn11.18:1.8: “Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation, and worshipped the different quarters.
sn11.18:1.9: Then Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka in verse:
sn11.18:2.1: “‘These all humbly worship you— Those versed in the Triple Veda,
sn11.18:2.2: All the khattiyas reigning on earth,
sn11.18:2.3: The Four Great Kings and the glorious Thirty—
sn11.18:2.5: So who, O Sakka, is that spirit
sn11.18:2.6: To whom you bow in worship?’ [Sakka:
sn11.18:3.1: “‘These all humbly worship me— Those versed in the Triple Veda,
sn11.18:3.2: All the khattiyas reigning on earth,
sn11.18:3.3: The Four Great Kings and the glorious Thirty—
sn11.18:4.1: But I worship those endowed with virtue,
sn11.18:4.3: Those who have properly gone forth
sn11.18:4.4: With the holy life their destination. “‘I worship as well, O Mātali,
sn11.18:5.2: The lay followers possessed of virtue
sn11.18:5.3: Who righteously maintain a wife.’ [Mātali: “‘Those whom you worship, my lord Sakka,
sn11.18:6.1: Are indeed the best in the world.
sn11.18:6.4: Those whom you worship, Vāsava.’ [The Blessed One:
sn11.18:7.1: “Having given this explanation, Having worshipped the different quarters,
sn11.18:7.4: The chief, climbed into his chariot.”
